| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Deployment-side detail REDACTED — the pass the previous event flagged. No decision, gate, open question, schema constraint or slice changed; what changed is what this entry stores about a running system. THE PRINCIPLE APPLIED, because it decides every individual call: the deployment data existed to establish a PROPERTY, not to serve as a list. D18 rejects an operator-side tolerance window on the ground that the fleet is ENUMERABLE, and what that argument consumes is size and shape — twelve instances over ten distinct modules, one cluster, one platform, three subscriptions. It never consumed the identities. So counts, shape and the structural facts that steer a runbook are kept in full, and the identifying enumeration is held out of band. WHAT WENT: research/migration-inventory.md's live-instance table (namespaces, instance names, module coordinates, and all twelve pre-migration instanceUUID values), its per-module deployed-version mapping in the GHCR section, its live-Platform table (the three filter.range constraint strings, the platform CR name and observedGeneration), and the namespace/coordinate table under `Finding first`; 06-operational.md's naming of the eight deployed modules and their local-versus-deployed skew, and the two runbook notes that identified instances by namespace and name; and D18's `Fleet measured 2026-07-27` line, which named two deployment repositories and five environments. WHAT STAYED, and why the document still works: every registry inventory (published artifacts are public by construction), the two-registry finding, the compiled-in --registry default and the resolveRegistry precedence defect, the spelling collision and its two-registry cleanup, the reserved-segment classes, the D8 rename finding, and the source-versus-registry reconciliation. The Method section keeps the exact commands, which is the point — this entry records the METHOD and the CONCLUSION, and the identifying data is re-derivable by anyone with cluster access rather than stored in a public repository. THREE FACTS SURFACED WHILE REDACTING, each recorded in generalised form rather than dropped. The positive-check subject D18 nominates — the fleet's only @v0 test artifact, `the cheapest subject because losing it costs nothing` — HAS BEEN REMOVED from the cluster since the 2026-07-30 measurement, so that gate needs a purpose-created throwaway instance instead; noted in both migration-inventory.md and 06-operational.md. The instance set is NOT STABLE between measurements (one added, one removed, one module upgraded across a minor between 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-05), so a runbook built from a fixed list is stale on arrival and the enumeration must be re-taken at execution time — which is independently an argument for not storing it. And the D14 platform rewrite has ONE NON-MECHANICAL STEP that the redacted table made visible: the subscription carrying 0006 A5's upper bound must collapse to the alpha it currently pins, not to the highest tag present, or the migration itself selects the `-dev` build that bound exists to exclude. 0011 WAS EXAMINED AND NEEDED NO EDIT: its D17 registry enumeration is repository counts and public artifact paths, and the entry carries no namespace, instance, UUID or environment identifier anywhere. Two coherence fixes made in passing, both created or exposed by this pass: migration-inventory.md §5's `single largest gap` item still said the fleet-facing registry was un-enumerated, which the 2026-07-31 GHCR read closed and the document's own header note already said; and its release-artifact class still cited 0011 D5 as needing a reserved segment, which 0011 D14 resolved out of scope. | Module and Catalog Identity |
| [0011](./0011/) | cli | accepted | minor | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Two cross-enhancement edges declared, closing a gap that would have broken this entry's own CI cutovers. No slice added, removed or renamed; all nine stand, and EVERY ONE IS SCHEMA, CODE OR DOCS — this entry contributes no migration work at all. That is not a judgement call: catalogs-publish-cutover and modules-publish-cutover change a release pipeline's CONFIGURATION and publish nothing themselves, so the two acts that change a published artifact are both 0010's. THE GAP: catalogs-publish-cutover points release.yml at `opm catalog publish`, and modules-publish-cutover points the modules pipeline at `opm module publish`. Under D21 both commands validate identity/identity.cue by unifying it against core's #IdentityPackage and REFUSE a tree where it is absent — that is refusal 10 in 06-operational.md, and D4 refuses a non-concrete one. On a pre-migration tree the refusal fires, so pointing CI at either command before the identity files exist replaces a working pipeline with a failing one. Neither slice declared a dependency on anything that creates those files; both now depend on 0010's new authoring slices (catalogs-publish-cutover -> 0010:catalogs-identity-authoring, modules-publish-cutover -> 0010:modules-identity-authoring). THIS IS ALSO WHAT FORCED 0010'S SPLIT, and the two are worth reading together: 0010 had bundled `commit the identity file` with `republish` in one slice per repo, so the only edge available would have made a CI configuration change depend on a fleet republish — putting an irreversible publish upstream of a reversible config edit, and making the schema/migration boundary unstateable. 0010 split those slices in the same pass; the edges point at the source-only halves. Four cross-enhancement edges now connect the pair, against the two declared yesterday. modules-publish-cutover's concern is corrected on the same point: it cited 0010's modules-fleet-republish as the owner of the identity file, which after the split is modules-identity-authoring. D17's holding is unchanged — 0010's step 6 is still the only fleet republish and this entry still contributes only the mechanism. SCOPE CALL RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT BOUNDS THIS ENTRY TOO (author, 2026-08-05): clusters and environments are out of both entries. For this entry that removes nothing already sliced, but it does settle the disposition of three things its own documents raise and leave unowned — D17's registry cleanup items 2-4, the legacy v1alpha1 deletion gated on the v0 -> v1 fleet migration, and the Zot cutover that D10's tag immutability and D11's authenticated writes both depend on. All three are handled outside these entries; 0010's plan.yaml header carries the list so the absence reads as deliberate rather than as an oversight. | Module and Catalog Publishing |

| [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
